# Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi (Pe 2)

**ID:** Pe 2
**Section:** Peṭakopadesa (pe)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0520m.nrf1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi* ("The Second Stage: The Pattern of the Dispensation") is the second chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa*. Secondary studies note that the text analyzes how a disciple's right view of the Buddha's teaching is rooted in two complementary forms of discernment: wisdom arising from what is heard (*sutamayī paññā*), which derives from the phrasing and wording of the doctrines taught, and wisdom arising from reflection (*cintāmayī paññā*), which develops through inward appropriate attention to their essential meaning [Gal 2003; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics].
